industry: Specialty Steel - SBQ bar, seamless mechanical tubing, billets, components (EAF, Canton OH)
drawdown_context: MTUS entered the 2025-05-15 cutoff window with a deep multi-quarter de-rating after a violent earnings collapse: FY24 net income cratered to $1.3M (vs $69.4M in FY23, $65.1M in FY22) on revenue -20.4% YoY ($1,362M -> $1,084M) and gross profit -47.6%. Q1 2025 then re-confirmed the slide (net income $1.3M vs $24.0M Q1 2024 = -94.6%; net sales -12.8%; A&D mix-share shrinking). The cyclical narrative is real (auto destock, scrap deflation), but the disclosure-level question is whether management acted with insider candor or insider self-protection. The R/f/M framework finds the latter pattern: a synchronized Nov-Dec 2024 wave of CEO/CFO/CAO/GC 10b5-1 adoptions stacked behind an accelerating trough buyback at $18.45 avg cost. The 'lying-detector' framework should flag this even though no going concern, no covenant breach, no material weakness exists.

[EY:] We have served as the Company's auditors since 2012. [Opinion dated Feb 27, 2025, Cleveland, Ohio] [ICFR:] unqualified opinion thereon.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: auditor_change_tracker + ICFR opinion + 8-K Item 4.01 history. Verify Big-4 tenure and clean control opinion, since this is the first-order 'is there an accounting blow-up coming?' check.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Ernst & Young (Big 4, PCAOB ID 42) auditor since 2012 = 13-year continuous tenure. Clean opinion on both financial statements and ICFR. No Item 9 disagreements. No 8-K Item 4.01 events. ICFR effective. No going concern language anywhere in the filing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A is genuinely clean on the audit and controls dimension. The 'lying' angle is NOT accounting fraud - earnings cratered honestly in the audited numbers. This passes the first filter and forces the framework to look at Mode B behavioral signals.

rfm_tuples.R: Net sales for the year ended December 31, 2024 were $1,084.0 million, a decrease of $278.4 million, or 20.4%, compared with the year ended December 31, 2023. [Comprehensive Income table:] Net income (loss) FY24 $1.3 [million] vs $69.4 [FY23] vs $65.1 [FY22]. Gross profit for the year ended December 31, 2024 decreased $88.8 million, or 47.6%, compared with the year ended December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: claim verification on the headline distress trajectory. Did GAAP net income to the parent really collapse by ~98% in a single year, and did Q1 2025 confirm rather than reverse the slide? Is the disclosure candid about cause (cyclical vs structural)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 NI = $1.3M (down -98.1% YoY from $69.4M). Q1 2025 NI = $1.3M (down -94.6% YoY from $24.0M). Two full year+quarter of GAAP earnings collapse. MD&A attributes Q1 2025 weakness to 'unfavorable price/mix... lower base prices across end-markets as well as a smaller proportion of aerospace & defense shipments' - A&D was the bright spot in FY24 (+17%) and that strength is fading in Q1. Volume only -2.3 thousand ship tons in Q1 (small) but base PRICE is rolling over - a structural/competitive read, not just a cycle.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: the company disclosed the cratering honestly (no euphemisms, GAAP not adjusted) but the trajectory is materially worse than 'cyclical destock' messaging. A&D was 17% UP in FY24 yet first-quarter aerospace mix is already SHRINKING - the one positive end-market is decelerating into the cutoff. This is moderate-severity because it's transparent, but the rate of decline is incompatible with 'through-cycle' framing.

rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar. The strongest Mode B 'lying' tell in the framework is a CLUSTER of officer 10b5-1 adoptions stacked behind a known catalyst window. Test for (a) coincident adoptions across the C-suite, (b) timing the sale start dates to land just after the 10-K release and (c) sell start dates timed to the disclosure window.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9B (Insider Trading Arrangements section) + cross-check on Q1 2025 10-Q (no new plans, confirming the cluster was the November/December wave)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FOUR officer plans adopted in 22 days (Nov 14, 16, 18, Dec 5, 2024) - CEO (100K shares), CFO (12K + 12,104 option shares), General Counsel/CHRO (15K), Chief Accounting Officer (22K). ALL FOUR have sale-start dates clustered in the FIRST WEEK OF MARCH 2025 (March 3, 6, 6, 6) and all four end by Sept 2025 - i.e., sales open within ~5 trading days of the 10-K filing (2/27/2025) and run through the next earnings cycle. The MGPI pilot established this exact fact pattern. The CFO's inclusion of OPTION EXERCISE + SALE (not just routine RSU sell-to-cover) is the strongest signal - option exercise is a deliberate cash-out, not a tax-mandated mechanic. Worth noting: aggregate share counts are modest (~149K shares of a ~44M float, ~0.3%), so the SIZE is not large; but the SYNCHRONIZATION + COMPOSITION is the tell.

rfm_tuples.R: On December 20, 2021 Metallus announced that its Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program... up to $50.0 million... On November 2, 2022... an additional $75.0 million... and on May 6, 2024 the Board of Directors authorized an additional $100.0 million. [FY24:] approximately 2.0 million common shares... aggregate cost of $37.6 million... average repurchase price of $18.45 per share. [FY23:] 1.7 million common shares... $32.6 million... $19.03 per share. [FY22:] 3.0 million common shares... $52.0 million... $17.18 per share. [Q1 2025:] approximately 0.4 million common shares at an aggregate cost of $5.6 million... average repurchase price of $14.23 per share. [Subsequent to 3/31/2025 through 4/30/2025:] 0.1 million additional common shares... aggregate cost of $1.2 million... average repurchase price of $12.47 per share.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: capital_allocation_tell + insider-arithmetic asymmetry. Are insiders SELLING (via 10b5-1) at a price BELOW the price the company is BUYING back at? And is the buyback ACCELERATING into the trough (the MGPI 'defend-the-print' pattern) or DECELERATING (the ANDE 'preserve-optionality' pattern)?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 12 Treasury Shares + Issuer Purchases table + Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A and Item 2
rfm_tuples.M_value: The Board RAISED the buyback authorization by $100M on May 6, 2024 - i.e., AS earnings were collapsing (FY24 NI ended at $1.3M). Buyback was active throughout FY24 ($37.6M / 2.0M sh @ $18.45). Buyback ACCELERATED through the trough: Q1 2025 ran ~$5.6M/quarter pace (annualized ~$22M), and April 2025 continued at $12.47/sh - i.e., management is buying at PROGRESSIVELY LOWER PRICES as the cycle deepens. Cumulative buyback $128M of $225M authorized. INSIDER-VS-COMPANY ARITHMETIC: officer 10b5-1 plans were adopted in Nov 2024 (then-price ~$15-16) with March 2025 sale windows; company was buying back at $18.45 (FY24 avg) - so the COMPANY paid a higher average price than the price insiders chose to start selling at. Asymmetric: insiders timed sales to a window when their shares could leave at LOWER prices than the company defended.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B 'defend-the-print' pattern PLUS insider arithmetic asymmetry. (1) The Board authorization was UPSIZED $100M two quarters into the earnings collapse, then deployed actively into the trough - classic 'subsidize the multiple' behavior. (2) Insiders adopted SELL plans at the bottom and timed sale start dates to the immediate post-10-K window. (3) The company's average $18.45 FY24 cost vs Q1 2025 $14.23 vs April $12.47 implies management was buying ahead of price discovery, NOT after; the trajectory of repurchase price tells you the company KNEW what was coming and tried to support before disclosure. The fact pattern mirrors the canonical bear MGPI sequence (Nov/Dec buyback acceleration before a derivative suit). Combined with C3, this is a SEVERE tell.

Does the funded amount line up with cumulative receipts ($53.5M + $11.9M = $65.4M / $99.75M = 65.6%)? Is the operational milestone language stable across the 10-K and 10-Q?

rfm_tuples.M_value: Cumulative receipts of $65.4M against $99.75M total commitment = 65.6% drawn through Feb 2025 (year 1 of agreement). Targeted operational dates: 'late 2025' for the continuous bloom reheat furnace and 'first half of 2026' for the roller hearth furnace. For the year ended December 31, 2024, sales to our 10 largest customers accounted for approximately 50% of our net sales.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: customer concentration check. (A) Does the 11.2% top customer satisfy disclosure thresholds? (B) Given the 10-largest = 50% structure, is the concentration meaningfully different from the prior-year disclosure (i.e., did one customer's share creep up as overall sales fell)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: One customer = 11.2% of net sales (~$121M) on a $1,084M revenue base. Top 10 = 50% (~$542M). The 10-K does not name the customer (typical for steel merchants) and does not give the prior-year top-customer percentage for a clean YoY comparison. Given net sales fell $278M (-20.4%) but only one customer crossed the 10% threshold, the structural concentration is moderate. The undisclosed item is whether the 11.2% customer is an automotive OEM (most likely given product mix), an A&D primes (Northrop/Lockheed via the Army contract chain), or an energy distributor - each has very different cyclical correlation with MTUS.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A is met (threshold disclosure complies); Mode B is unverifiable in the blinding window because (i) prior 10-K's top-customer share is not on hand and (ii) the customer name is withheld. The framework cannot upgrade this to a flag without the comparative data; mark UNVERIFIABLE and note that customer concentration is a latent risk if the 11.2% customer is auto-OEM (the end-market doing worst in Q1 2025).

rfm_tuples.M_value: Maturity wall: $46M Convertible Senior Notes due Dec 1, 2025 (~7 months post-cutoff) - material but covered: ABL availability is $251.7M (3/31/2025) and total cash interest paid in 2024 was only $2.0M (low absolute leverage). Credit Facility matures Sept 30, 2027 (no near-term refinancing pressure). Springing FCC covenant has not been triggered (availability remains well above the threshold). MTUS pension contribution Q1 2025 alone was $52.6M - significant cash drain that is being funded from operations and cash on hand, not from the ABL. The conv note can either be settled in cash from existing liquidity or, given the trigger price ($25.51 conversion price vs ~$12-14 spot), will simply be paid off in cash at par.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A passes on the credit/covenant dimension. The $46M conv-2025 maturity is a near-term but well-managed event (more than 5x covered by ABL availability before drawing). This is the cleanest part of the disclosure and is a genuine structural backstop - it's why the framework cannot SHORT this name purely on the earnings trajectory. The combination of clean credit and a US Army capex grant create real downside protection.

The Contract covers approximately 1,170 bargaining employees at the Company's Canton, Ohio operations.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: labor_calendar_overlay. The USW contract expires Sept 27, 2025 - i.e., 4.5 months after the cutoff and 4 months before the conv-note maturity. Is the company silent about renewal status, or do they signal contingency planning? The 10-K's silence on contingency would be a Mode B tell.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 Human Capital + Item 1A Risk Factors + Q1 2025 10-Q (no incremental disclosure)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K Item 1A flags labor relations as a generic risk but does NOT describe renewal preparations, mediation status, or strike-contingency planning for the Sept 2025 contract expiration. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/8/2025, just 4.5 months from expiration) has ZERO incremental disclosure on USW renewal status. The 4.5-month silence in a Q1 filing is itself a Mode B signal - companies that have constructive talks usually telegraph it.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: a 1,170-employee USW contract at the SOLE producing facility (Canton, OH) expiring 4.5 months post-cutoff, with the Q1 2025 10-Q completely silent on renewal status, is a latent operational risk that should have at minimum a one-sentence acknowledgment. Combined with the synchronized officer 10b5-1 cluster (C3), the silence is consistent with management preferring not to flag what could be a Q3/Q4 2025 operational event (strike, work stoppage, costly settlement) ahead of insider sale windows. Not red-flag alone, but consistent with the broader Mode B pattern.

rfm_tuples.M_value: A&D is one of FOUR roughly equal end-markets (industrial, auto, A&D, energy). The 10-K says A&D shipments rose ~17% in 2024 - strong but A&D is still a minority of revenue. The rename and Army contract were announced one day apart (Feb 26 and Feb 27, 2024). Then in Q1 2025, A&D mix-share is already SHRINKING ('a smaller proportion of aerospace & defense shipments' is cited as a Q1 sales-decline driver). So the defense-pivot brand story telegraphed in Feb 2024 has not played out in Q1 2025's actual mix - the company is reverting back to being a cyclical SBQ steel producer with auto/industrial exposure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the rebrand+Army-contract bundle was a narrative pivot to capture defense-thematic investor flows, but Q1 2025 results show A&D mix-share is now FALLING. The 10-K does not quantify what % of FY24 revenue was A&D, so an investor cannot independently judge how much of the company is actually a 'defense' name versus a cyclical steel name dressed up as one. The disclosure stack is not lying but is letting the brand do work that the mix data does not support.

The 'most of which related to the Bargaining Plan' phrasing suggests defunding the union pension liability ahead of the Sept 2025 USW contract expiration - a defensive move that drains liquidity but reduces post-renegotiation pension demands. supplemental_signals.framework_call_rationale: The R/f/M framework reads INSIDER BEHAVIOR + CAPITAL ALLOCATION (Mode B signals C3 and C4) as the strongest discrimination signal even when the audit/covenant stack is clean. MTUS exhibits the canonical 'officers diversify + company defends multiple at lower prices' pattern that the smallcap pilot established as the strongest forward-return tell. The structural offsets (clean credit, Army contract, pension discipline) keep this from being SHORT-tier; the behavioral cluster keeps it from being LONG-tier.

summary: MTUS is a NEUTRAL-to-SHORT-leaning name where the audit/covenant/credit dimension is genuinely clean (EY since 2012, ICFR effective, no going concern, $251.7M ABL availability vs $46M conv-note maturity Dec 2025, U.S. Army $99.75M capex grant providing 2026 throughput catalyst), but the BEHAVIORAL Mode B stack lights up multiple framework tells in coordinated fashion. FY24 GAAP net income collapsed 98% YoY ($69.4M -> $1.3M) on a -20.4% revenue decline, and Q1 2025 re-confirmed the slide (NI $1.3M vs $24.0M, -94.6%). The key disclosure-level tells: (1) FOUR officer 10b5-1 plans were adopted in a 22-day window Nov 14 - Dec 5, 2024 - CEO Williams (100K sh), CFO Westbrooks (12K + 12,104 option-exercise shares), EVP GC/CHRO Syrvalin (15K sh), CAO Yacobozzi (22K sh) - all with sale-start dates clustered in the FIRST WEEK OF MARCH 2025 (~5 trading days after the 10-K filing), all ending Sept 2025 ahead of the next earnings cycle; the CFO plan affirmatively exercises options and sells (not tax-cover). (2) The Board UPSIZED the buyback authorization by $100M on May 6, 2024 - during the earnings collapse - and deployed it at PROGRESSIVELY LOWER PRICES ($18.45 FY24 avg -> $14.23 Q1 2025 -> $12.47 April 2025), the classic 'defend-the-print at sequentially lower marks' bear pattern (mirrors MGPI Nov/Dec 2024 derivative-suit fact pattern). Insiders chose to start selling at prices BELOW where the company was buying - asymmetric arithmetic against shareholders. (3) USW Local 1123 contract covering 1,170 employees at the sole Canton OH facility expires September 27, 2025, but the Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/8/2025, just 4.5 months out) is completely silent on renewal status - a Mode B 'don't flag what insider sales will sit through' silence. (4) The TimkenSteel -> Metallus rebrand happened one day before signing the U.S. Army contract - narrative-pivot timing that has not been validated by Q1 2025 results (A&D mix-share is now SHRINKING). The framework can't push this to SHORT-tier because: clean Big-4 audit, no covenant breach, fully covered conv-note maturity, real US Army contract catalyst, $251.7M ABL undrawn. But the behavioral cluster around the disclosure window is exactly what the honesty-alpha framework is designed to detect - composite should land in MODERATE-NEGATIVE territory (~0.55-0.70 range), short-tier-eligible.
